sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. TransNewGuinea.org: Kosare (lexicon; source Heeschen 1978).

Heeschen, Volker. 1978. The Mek languages of Irian Jaya with special reference to the Eipo language. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development 7(2): 3-46 (Kosare: p.5; Kosare wordlist, Appendix pp. 41-44).
sources.note: Nothing for Kosare. The Appendix intro only says the Kosare transcription is 'somewhat narrower'; the 97-item Kosare list carries per-word stress marks ('kako 'bone', 'tomo 'black', kora'fe 'one', o'reka 'kill', to'wai 'know') but no rule is stated. (Stress/tone remarks on pp. 10-11, 20-21 concern the Mek languages, not Kosare.)

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. New Guinea World: Nawa River (Kaure-Kosare family page: situation, sources, historical phonology).
sources.note: States 'There is no published phonology of Kosare.' Proposes a 12-consonant / 7-vowel inventory by comparing Heeschen 1978 and Wambaliau 2006 wordlists with Kaure; reproduces both wordlists with their stress marks (Wambaliau: kaˈkuʔ, tuˈmuʔ, pɔˈtɔʔ, aiˈmuʔ, kuɽaˈpɛ, uɭɛˈka but ˈmijɛ, ˈwi-); no stress rule stated.
